title: "Setup"
---

## On HTCF (spack)

**R and system libraries** come from the spack environment
`/ref/mblab/software/chasem/spack_envs/rstudio-4.6.1`. It's the one `rstudio_spack.sbatch`
launches RStudio Server from, so an RStudio session on the cluster already has it. Outside
RStudio, activate it the way `run_pipeline.sbatch` does:

```sh
SPACK_ENV=/ref/mblab/software/chasem/spack_envs/rstudio-4.6.1
eval "$(spack env activate --sh "$SPACK_ENV")"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$SPACK_ENV/view/lib:$SPACK_ENV/view/lib64${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
unset R_LIBS R_LIBS_USER R_LIBS_SITE
```

`spack env activate` doesn't set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and packages compiled against the
environment's libraries need it. Unsetting `R_LIBS*` keeps other libraries off the path, so
the project's renv library is the only one in use.

**R packages** come from the project's renv library (`renv.lock`). renv activates
automatically from `.Rprofile` when R starts in the project directory. From a fresh clone:

```r
options(renv.install.timeout = 6 * 3600)
renv::restore()
```

- **The timeout.** Everything builds from source against the spack libraries (roughly 300
  packages, hours of build time). renv's default deadline for a whole install is one hour,
  and when it's reached renv rolls back the entire batch. Finished builds stay in renv's
  cache, so a re-run picks up where it stopped.
- **`.Rprofile` turns off two renv start-up checks**, `synchronized.check` (a scan of every
  project file, about a minute on `/scratch`) and the sandbox (about 40 s on `~/.cache` when
  20 workers start at once). Together they took every worker's R start-up from 68 s to about
  10 s. Run `renv::status()` by hand when you want the check.

### Two packages that need care

**CoGAPS is installed from a patched local checkout, not a repository.** Its committed
`configure` leaves the autoconf-archive OpenMP macros unexpanded
([FertigLab/CoGAPS#150](https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS/issues/150)), so built as-is it
compiles single-threaded without saying so. The upstream fix
([#151](https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS/pull/151)) only changes their Dockerfile, so
regenerate `configure` before installing:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FertigLab/CoGAPS.git logs/build/CoGAPS
git -C logs/build/CoGAPS checkout f9075096   # master as installed (3.33.2), after #151
export ACLOCAL_PATH="$(spack location -i autoconf-archive)/share/aclocal"
(cd logs/build/CoGAPS && autoreconf -fi)
Rscript -e 'renv::install(normalizePath("logs/build/CoGAPS"))'
Rscript -e 'library(CoGAPS); stopifnot(compiledWithOpenMPSupport())'
```

Without spack, install `autoconf-archive` however the system provides it and point
`ACLOCAL_PATH` at its `aclocal` directory.

**projectR is the `feature-add_center_by_loadings` branch of
[cmatKhan/projectR](https://github.com/cmatKhan/projectR/tree/feature-add_center_by_loadings).**
It adds `center_by_loadings`, used to project PCA fits. renv records it as a GitHub remote,
so `renv::restore()` installs it.

## Raw data

Dataset configs give data paths relative to a data root: `data_root` in
`config/pipeline.yml` (`/scratch/mblab/chasem/hf_sepsis_collection` on HTCF), overridden by
the `SEPSIS_DATA_ROOT` environment variable. See [Data](data.qmd).

## Running elsewhere (without spack, or another scheduler)

Nothing in the pipeline depends on spack. Only two places put R on the path:
`config/pipeline.yml` for the workers, and `run_pipeline.sbatch` for the main process. On
another SLURM cluster:

1. Get R 4.6 however the cluster provides it, e.g. `module load R/4.6.1`, and run
   `renv::restore()` once in the project.
2. In `config/pipeline.yml`, give the workers' setup lines in place of the spack
   activation:
   ```yaml
   cluster:
     setup_lines: ["module load R/4.6.1"]
     partition: <your partition, or null>
   ```
3. In `run_pipeline.sbatch`, replace the spack activation lines with the same `module load`.
4. Point `data_root` (or `SEPSIS_DATA_ROOT`) at that machine's copy of the data.

This mirrors the `script_lines = "module load R"` example in crew.cluster's documentation.
For SGE, PBS or LSF clusters, swap `crew_controller_slurm()`/`crew_options_slurm()` in
`R/targets/controllers.R` for crew.cluster's `_sge`/`_pbs`/`_lsf` equivalents. To run on one
machine, use `crew::crew_controller_local()`. crew.cluster labels itself
Experimental/Maturing; targets and crew are mature.

## Building these docs

The site is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website in `docs/`. Quarto ships with RStudio
Server (`.../rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto`); elsewhere, install it from quarto.org.

```sh
quarto render docs      # writes docs/_site/
quarto preview docs     # live preview while editing
```

Rendering first runs `docs/build_reference.R`, which builds the
[Function reference](reference.qmd) from the roxygen comments in the code (it needs the
project's `roxygen2`).

### Documenting functions

Every function carries a standard [roxygen](https://roxygen2.r-lib.org) block: a title line,
a description, `@param` for each argument and `@return`. This is a project, not a package,
so there are no `man/` pages; the blocks feed the reference page instead.

```r
#' Stable identity for a fit
#'
#' Dataset + method + parameters, excluding resource-only settings.
#'
#' @param dataset_id Dataset id.
#' @param method Method name.
#' @param params Flattened parameter list (`flatten_params()`).
#' @param resource_params Parameter names left out of the identity.
#' @return The fit key, `"<method>_<16 hex characters>"`.
fit_key <- function(dataset_id, method, params, resource_params = character(0)) { ... }
```

Comments never change targets' hashes, so documenting a function never reruns anything.
